title: Colorado PUC Decision C26-0041: Commission Decision Denying Temporary Authority
text:
Decision No. C26-0041 
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF COLORADO 
PROCEEDING NO. 26A-0033CP-ETA 
IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EMERALD EXPRESS TRANSPORTATION, 
INC. FOR EMERGENCY TEMPORARY AUTHORITY TO OPERATE AS A COMMON 
CARRIER BY MOTOR VEHICLE FOR HIRE. 
COMMISSION DECISION DENYING 
TEMPORARY AUTHORITY 
Issued Date: 
January 16, 2026 
Adopted Date: January 14, 2026 

I. 
BY THE COMMISSION 
A. 
Statement, Findings, and Conclusions 
1. 
On January 5, 2025, Emerald Express Transportation, Inc. (“Emerald Express”) 
filed an Application for Emergency Temporary Authority1 to Operate as a Common Carrier of 
Passengers by Motor Vehicle for Hire (“Application”). 
2. 
Emerald Express, in this Application, requests emergency temporary authority for 
30 days as follows: 
(1) Transportation of passengers in call-and-demand shuttle service 
between all points within the city of Steamboat Springs, Colorado, and 
between said points, on the one hand, and the Yampa Valley Regional 
Airport, Hayden, Colorado, on the other hand. (2) Transportation of 
passengers in call-and-demand shuttle service between all points within the 

1 Emerald Express Transportation filed an Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and 
Necessity to operate as a common carrier of passengers on May 19, 2025, in Proceeding 25A-0202CP. 
The permanent authority requested in Proceeding 25A-0202CP is the same as in Proceeding 
26A-0033CP-ETA. Alpine Taxi/Limo, Inc. and NDW Enterprises LLC, doing business as Ski Town 
Transportation, filed Interventions by Right to the permanent authority application. An evidentiary hearing 
was scheduled for December 2-4, 2025, by Decision No. R25-0778-I. As of January 14, 2026, the 
administrative law judge assigned to o Proceeding 25A-0202CP has not issued a recommended decision 
granting or denying the permanent application.

Decision No. C26-0041

2 
city of Craig, Colorado, and between said points, on the one hand, and the 
Yampa Valley Regional Airport, Hayden, Colorado, on the other hand. 
3. 
Pursuant to § 40-10.1-204(1), C.R.S., the Commission is authorized to grant 
temporary authority when “there appears to be an immediate and urgent need to any point or within 
a territory having no such service capable of meeting the need.” Section 40-10.1-204(4), C.R.S., 
further states: “If the Commission determines that an emergency exists, it may issue temporary 
authority or approval at once by making specific reference in its order to the circumstances 
constituting the emergency, in which case no notice need be given, but any such emergency 
authority or approval expires no later than thirty days after it was issued.” 
4. 
Therefore, Emerald Express must meet a two-fold test: first, that there is an 
immediate and urgent need for the transportation services, and second, that there is no existing 
carrier capable of meeting the need. If Emerald Express fails to meet either test, the Application 
must be denied. 
5. 
Rule 6204(b) of the Rules Regulating Transportation by Motor Vehicle, 4 Code of 
Colorado Regulations (“CCR”) 723-6 states: 
(b) A Person may seek emergency temporary Authority to operate as a 
Common or Contract Carrier for a period not to exceed 30 days and shall 
file an application with the Commission providing the information in 
paragraph (a) of this rule. The application shall also include a statement of 
facts establishing the basis and nature of the emergency need for the 
proposed service. Any letters of support shall describe the basis and nature 
of the emergency. 
6. 
In support of the emergency temporary authority application, Emerald Express 
Transportation states the following: 
Yampa Valley Regional Airport (“YVRA” or the “Airport”) is a critical 
regional transportation hub that provides year-round commercial air 
service, business jet operations, general aviation access, air cargo, and 
medical evacuation support for Northwest Colorado communities, 
including Steamboat Springs and Craig. Since 2021, YVRA has 
experienced sustained and unprecedented growth in commercial airline 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. C26-0041 
PROCEEDING NO. 26A-0033CP-ETA 
3 
traffic. Six major airlines now provide direct winter-season flights between 
YBRA and sixteen major U.S. airports, resulting in significant increases in 
total passenger volume, including during the current winter season both at 
present and anticipated. This rapid and significant expansion has increased 
the public need for and reliance on ground transportation from the resort 
community of Steamboat Springs, as well as the need for transportation to 
and from Craig (where many local workers reside). Recently, one of the two 
existing CPCN holders serving the YVRA in call and demand shuttle 
service (i.e. providing “walk up” transportation), Alpine Taxi/Limo 
(aka Steamboat Express) was banned from serving the Airport after it a) 
pulled out of its counter service and b) became embroiled in a contract 
dispute with the Airport. Alpine was also, on information and belief, 
suffering from operational and financial instability. Alpine has represented 
that it does not intend to re-open a counter at YVRA, and it is currently 
involved in a dispute before the PUC regarding its ban from Airport 
premises, but by its own admission it is currently unable to serve the 
YVRA2. As a result, only one certified ground transportation provider 
remains available to meet the needs of thousands of arriving and departing 
passengers each week. 
7. 
The CEO, Sarah Leonard, of the Steamboat Springs Chamber wrote a letter of 
support for Emerald Express’ ETA application on December 17, 2025. In the letter Ms. Leonard 
states: 
On behalf of the Steamboat Springs Chamber, I’m writing to share our 
formal support for Emerald Express Transportation’s request for 
Emergency and Temporary Common Carrier Authority. With winter air 
service already begun, our community is facing an immediate and 
significant shortage of walk-up ground transportation at the Yampa Valley 
Regional Airport (YVRA) making this request time sensitive for our 
community. As we noted in our earlier correspondence and outlined in my 
recent testimony on behalf of Emerald Express in Proceeding 24A-0202CP, 
the closure of Alpine Taxi/Limo (aka Steamboat Express)’s airport 
operations created a substantial gap in shared transportation options for 
residents and visitors flying into YVRA. Today, only one authorized walk-
up provider remains at YVRA—an arrangement that currently does not 

2 Alpine Taxi/Limo, Inc. ("Alpine Taxi") filed a Petition for Declaratory Order ("Petition") with 
the Colorado Public Utility Commission (“Commission”) on October 15, 2025. In the Petition, Alpine Taxi 
is seeking an order from the Commission addressing whether Yampa Valley Regional Airport (“YVRA”) 
has the authority to bar Alpine Taxi from serving YVRA. The Commission accepted the Petition and 
referred it to an administrative law judge by Decision C25-0791 on November 4, 2025, in Proceeding No. 
25D-0435CP. On December 4, 2025, Routt County filed a Motion to Intervene of Right or in the Alternative 
Motion for Leave to Intervene. Routt County was acknowledged as a party of right on December 22, 2025, 
in Decision No. R25-0920-I.

4 
meet the needs of winter travelers, particularly during peak arrival windows 
and challenging weather. Reliable airport transportation is an essential part 
of the Steamboat Springs visitor experience. Our hotels, restaurants, 
retailers, event venues, and local businesses depend on safe, predictable 
access for guests and employees alike. When ground transportation falls 
short, those impacts ripple throughout our community, affecting visitor 
satisfaction, reliability, and the overall strength of our economy. Steamboat 
Springs relies on positive experiences and return visitation to sustain our 
busy winter season. 
8. 
The Commission is aware that NDW Enterprises, LLC doing business as Ski Town 
Transportation (“Ski Town”) was issued Certificate No. 55991 on July 19, 2023, by Decision No. 
R23-0302 in Proceeding No. 22A-0132CP. Certificate No. 55991 authorizes Ski Town to provide 
shuttle service (a) between the YRVA and all points in Steamboat Springs, Colorado and all points 
within one mile of the city limits of Steamboat Springs; and (b) between the YRVA and all points 
in Craig, Colorado. 
9. 
The Commission is also aware that Steamboat Shuttle Service, LLC, doing 
business as Steamboat Shuttle Service (“Steamboat Shuttle Service”) was granted authority on 
December 19, 2025, to provide call-and demand shuttle service and call-and-demand charter 
service between all points in Routt County by Decision No. C25-0914 in Proceeding 25A-0454CP. 
Steamboat Shuttle Service has not completed the compliance requirements named in Decision No. 
C25-0914. The Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (“CPCN”) to operate as a 
common carrier of passengers will not be issued to Steamboat Shuttle Service until the compliance 
requirements are completed. 
10. 
The Commission finds that while the statements provided by the owner of 
Emerald Express Transportation and the CEO of the Steamboat Springs Chamber may support the 
need for additional passenger carriers during the winter season, these statements do not meet the 
standards of showing an immediate and urgent need as required by § 40-10.1-204 (1), C.R.S and 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. C26-0041 
PROCEEDING NO. 26A-0033CP-ETA 
5 
an emergency need for the proposed service as required by Rule 6204(b), 4 CCR 723-6. 
Considering that there is common carrier service available within the requested geographic area 
and that Emerald Express has not shown an immediate and urgent need, the Commission finds that 
the information submitted with the Application does not support the granting of emergency 
temporary authority. Thus, this application for emergency temporary authority is not in the public 
interest and will be denied. 
11. 
The denial of this Application creates no presumption about the final disposition of 
a temporary or permanent authority application filed by Emerald Express. 
II. 
ORDER 
A. 
The Commission Orders That: 
1. 
The application for emergency temporary authority filed on January 5, 2026, by 
Emerald Express Transportation, Inc. is denied, consistent with the discussion above. 
2. 
The 20-day time period provided by § 40-6-114(1), C.R.S., to file an Application 
for Rehearing, Reargument, or Reconsideration shall begin on the first day following the effective 
date of this Decision.
